audit_kind: informed independent whole-style development audit; no quality scores

inspection_method.display: Each image was returned and visually inspected separately as a full image, with its exact path labelled. No contact sheets or newly made crops were used.
inspection_method.ordering: Request and rejection were read before image viewing. Poster batches M1 through M5 preceded all source JPEGs. The five source JPEGs and whole-reference-note.md preceded the runtime reading. Within independent view batches, image results were emitted in the order recorded below; this is not a claim about concurrent tool completion timestamps.
inspection_method.native_semantics: The native view actually opened was final.png. Read-only byte comparison verified it equals original.png for all five selected stages. original.png was not a separate visual opening.
inspection_method.metadata_method: Read-only Python standard-library SHA-256 and PNG/JPEG header parsing; no resampling, rewriting or image generation. An initial Pillow import was unavailable, so the metadata check used standard-library parsing.

actual_poster_views.observation: Large white schedule/place/entry/application blocks occupy the teal left field. Heavy dark title and subtitle sit on the yellow right field; a rectangular sunlit exhibition-tour photograph is contained between title and two reassuring lines. Adults facing a guide and framed architectural photographs connect the event's two activities.

The practical copy is visually accessible in clearly separated groups. The large title and date/time compete as prominent anchors; the photograph remains an inset within the two-field announcement structure.
The teal/yellow split and dense bold text blocks remain the organizing impression. The warm group photograph is visible but does not reorganize the overall template.

A full-frame room, tall window, framed architectural photographs, wooden chairs and diagonal floor light establish depth. White copy uses darker side walls; the large two-line Korean title is at left, and the practical information is grouped at right. The light and chairs carry a quiet, contemplative mood.

The title is strong, but the window/light/chairs remain a coherent spatial subject. Practical information is visually readable on the darker wall regions, with smaller and lighter copy than the other selected posters.

Window brightness, floor-light diagonals and chairs retain a recognizable scene. The title remains an anchor; the smallest practical lines are not a claim of thumbnail readability. This is a meaningful scene-led counterexample to a blanket flat-field or sans-serif prohibition.

A large rectangular room/window photograph at left and a smaller sill detail crop at right are mounted on pale blue. An orange heavy title anchors the lower left. Very large date/time and dark place/entry/application/reassurance groups occupy the right. The detail crop repeats the same spatial subject rather than introducing another event action.

Practical groups are visually accessible, but the mounted-photo/editorial grid and bold title/date blocks determine the reading structure. The main photo is substantial; this is not accurately described as a tiny-icon-only output.

The title/date and two-column panel structure remain dominant graphic signals. The window and sill crops read as related views, while the palette alone would not establish a wholly different expression system from the other announcement layouts.

A central isometric cutaway illustrates seated adults listening to a speaker beside framed architectural photographs and window light. Warm masonry/wood, muted clothes and pale paper create an approachable instructional impression. Bold title/date and ruled information sections flank the scene on ivory.

The illustrated shared event remains identifiable, with readable practical groups at left and right. The drawing is substantial and semantically relevant, while the surrounding headline/information sections still read as independent panels.

The cutaway room survives as a central image shape, but three separate image/text zones remain. This is the important borderline example for an image-presence or image-area shortcut; the drawing's existence alone cannot settle the whole-style question.

A near-ivory upper field contains large dark title, subtitle, date/time and information groups in two columns. An independent lower graphic band shows repeated perspective windows and bright yellow light planes on navy. The hard-edged repetition conveys architectural light, but the exhibition-and-talk connection is carried mainly by the text.

The practical text remains easy to locate, and the lower illustration is conspicuous. The upper announcement panel and lower graphic strip remain separated rather than forming one edited spatial composition.

The large text panel above a graphic band remains the overall impression. Material, contrast and geometry differ from the realistic scenes, but adding a substantial bottom band does not itself escape the rejected template.

actual_source_views.observation: A stepped chain of unequal, overlapping photographic crops follows a helmeted woman's changing expressions in a tandem skydiving scene. Large white space is organized by the sequence; bold sans-serif title/credits run vertically along the far left. actual_source_views.transfer_limit: Do not copy the woman, jump sequence, exact crops, logos or film copy; temporal variation in this image is not evidence that the architecture event has a supplied timeline.

actual_source_views.observation: Large black and turquoise portrait contours of different scales overlap; a white brushed area, handwritten document field and scattered archival family photographs build a page-wide memory/puzzle relationship. A strong top sans-serif title and compact lower credits serve different roles from the portraits. The paper/ink texture belongs to the layered imagery rather than merely dressing a text card.

actual_source_views.observation: Very large cropped black boots frame a small receding figure and helmet in an orange-red illustrated scene. Ink hatching, shadow, depth and severe scale contrast organize the limited-colour field; a small top label and outlined lower title use the scene's edges. The image creates tension and force, unlike the approachable neighborhood-event tone.
actual_source_views.transfer_limit: Transfer the principle of meaningful scale/crop and information at a scene boundary, not its palette, boots, character, logo or threatening emotion.

limitations: This audit knows the original request, later preference and N guidance; it is informed development, not blind evaluation or a replacement judgment on the frozen R13 quality gates.
No fresh N images were produced or reviewed. Runtime compliance, reliability and transfer to new requests are untested here.
The files were viewed with original-detail image output, but actual venue screen size, viewing distance, luminance and print suitability were not tested.
Native poster dimensions are 1672×941, close to but not mathematically exact 16:9. Usage and thumbnail files are 720×405 and 320×180. Nothing was cropped or normalized in this audit.
Observations of copy access are visual whole-style observations, not independent blind transcription, Unicode authentication or a complete copy-accuracy certification.
Full JPEG pixels support visual expression observations, not certainty about physical manufacturing technique, AI usage or archival/factual provenance.
The source reference note was read; acquisition JSONs, existing root view logs, original critic results and peer reports were not used.
The native alias byte equality and hashes establish file identity; they are not substitutes for the explicitly recorded image viewing events.
